finding.claim: MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH is not enforced on chunked or streamed request bodies, so an unauthenticated client can force unbounded in-memory buffering. The buffered path only checks size after the whole body is queued.
finding.source: HTTP request body of any unauthenticated request sent with Transfer-Encoding: chunked or without Content-Length (src/quart/asgi.py:64-65).
finding.sink: Request body buffer capped by MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH (default 16 MB, src/quart/app.py:230); unbounded asyncio.Queue in Body.put (src/quart/wrappers/request.py:110-111).

trace.note: handle_messages puts every http.request chunk into request.body with no size check
Only up-front check compares declared Content-Length to the limit; chunked requests have none
__anext__ streams chunks with no max_content_length check
Multipart parsing iterates body via async for, bypassing the buffered check
Buffered __await__ accumulates the full body before checking length
Length check runs only after data is already buffered, too late to prevent the memory spike

finding.guards_checked: Content-Length precheck (request.py:65-70) is bypassed by chunked encoding; per-chunk limit absent in __anext__ (request.py:75-82); post-buffer check (request.py:102-106) runs after memory is consumed; BODY_TIMEOUT (asgi.py:97) limits idle time, not fast senders; max_form_memory_size (formparser.py:211-214) is off by default and covers non-file fields only. Unverified: whether werkzeug MultipartDecoder second argument (formparser.py:187-188) bounds total upload size; werkzeug not present in sandbox.
